transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Lena (Quantum Bridge), Markus (SRE), Priya (ML), Chris (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick discovery touching SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy approaches, quotas, and observability. Follow ups: send pricing, sample code, schedule deep dive.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate it. can we do quick intros?
00:06 Lena: hey i'm lena, head of platform at quantum bridge, we run payments infra and ML features for risk scoring.
00:12 Markus: markus, s r e, i'll be owning reliability part.
00:16 Priya: priya, ml engineering, we own the langchain stacks.
00:20 Chris: chris from procurement, i'll handle contract questions.
00:25 Jordan: great. samira and i are at redwood, samira's our solutions engineer who will do the deep dive. so high level, what's your eval criteria? latency, cost, security?
00:38 Lena: yeah all of that. we currently call openai for embeddings and chat but costs are getting high; we want more control and predictability. key musts: SSO, audit logs, on-prem option for data residency, and KMS for key management.
00:55 Samira: makes sense. quick question on your stack — you mentioned langchain, are you using LlamaIndex at all?
01:02 Priya: yes both. langchain for orchestration, llama index for vector store adapters and retrieval. we run both in k8s; proxies sit in front of model endpoints.
01:12 Jordan: ok so integration questions typically are SDKs, langchain connectors, and gateway/proxy patterns. do you have a preferred integration model — server-side proxy or direct from backend?
01:22 Markus: we're leaning proxy so we can centralize rate limiting and observability. we need a sidecar/gateway that can add tokens and enforce quotas.
01:31 Samira: redwood supports both: our SDKs are simple server-side clients for hosted; for dedicated/private we provide a customer gateway pattern — either a reverse-proxy or a local gateway that talks to the redwood control plane.
01:44 Priya: how opinionated are the SDKs re: langchain? any prebuilt chains?
01:49 Samira: we have official SDKs in python and node with adapters — and a LangChain integration repo that contains prompt templates, chain wrappers and examples for LlamaIndex. it's not tightly coupled, more like helper utilities.
01:59 Jordan: we'll share links — there is a public repo and an example that shows streaming and function calls with LangChain.
02:06 Lena: can you do a quick sketch of the gateway? do you host it or we run it?
02:11 Samira: for hosted customers you call the hosted API directly or through your proxy; for dedicated you typically run a small gateway in your VPC that routes to dedicated pools. private/on-prem is fully customer-run; the control plane can be private or we can provide an air-gapped bundle.
02:28 Markus: what about network egress and data residency — we need to keep tokens in region and not egress to us-east always.
02:35 Samira: you can pin regions with dedicated pools and private deployments can be entirely in your VPC/region. for hosted we have region selection and fallback policies — we'll document exact endpoints.
02:46 Priya: a big question: can we keep the KV cache and embeddings in our infra or does redwood cache on their side?
02:54 Samira: caching is configurable. for hosted there's prefix/KV caching at the edge for efficiency; you can opt out or provide your own cache when using a private deployment. for dedicated we can set up local caching on the GPU nodes in your VPC.
03:10 Jordan: and observability — what hooks do you provide for tracing and token-level cost?
03:15 Samira: we expose per-request headers for trace ids and have a tracing hook that integrates with Jaeger/Zipkin. console has token-level cost breakdowns and model route dashboards — plus a webhook for error events and custom metrics export through Prometheus.
03:31 Markus: retention of logs — need at least 1 year for audit.
03:35 Samira: retention is configurable for private/dedicated. hosted has tiers; we can discuss an enterprise retention add-on.
03:44 Lena: rate limits — we need per-API-key quotas, burst controls, and a way to smooth traffic. can we throttle by route?
03:53 Samira: yes per-key quotas, per-route limits, and you can define burst windows. we also offer client-side token bucket libraries in the SDK to smooth requests and a gateway policy engine for more advanced rules.
04:07 Priya: ok on the embeddings side, vector size and throughputs — can we run our own vector store (we use pinecone currently) and only use redwood for the model?
04:16 Samira: absolutely — you can use your vector store and call redwood for embeddings/generation; we support embedding-only endpoints and can return raw vectors. if you want internal routing, we can also host the embedding workloads on dedicated pools.
04:29 Jordan: any constraints for LlamaIndex connectors? e.g., batch sizes, streaming?
04:34 Samira: connectors are built to respect batching; streaming for generation is supported but LlamaIndex may buffer — the example repo shows recommended batch sizes and concurrency settings. we'll include a small benchmark script.
04:44 Markus: on security, SSO/SAML support? RBAC?
04:48 Samira: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, RBAC with roles, audit logs, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/HSM). for private we can integrate with your HSM.
05:00 Chris: procurement question, what's the contract cadence for dedicated — monthly or annual commitments?
05:06 Jordan: dedicated is typically reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits; we can structure flexible burst credits. I'll share the pricing doc.
05:14 Lena: do you have any customers with a similar compliance profile?
05:18 Samira: yes a couple of fintechs and payments companies; we can share redacted references and SOC2 report.
05:24 Priya: for the deep dive we want a performance benchmark: 2k tps for small embeddings, P95 latency under 200ms for short prompts. can you run a quick pilot?
05:35 Jordan: we can do a short pilot on dedicated — samira can coordinate the benchmark script.
05:39 Samira: i'll prepare a small benchmark harness that you can run in your environment hitting dedicated or hosted endpoints, include langchain examples.
05:45 Lena: timeline — we're aiming for a Q2 pilot and potential production by late Q2 if results are good.
05:51 Jordan: great. recap and next steps?
05:55 Lena: send pricing, security docs, langchain/llamaindex snippets, schedule week of march 8 for technical deep dive.
06:03 Jordan: yep jordan will send pricing, samira will drop code + benchmark, lena will send traffic profile.
06:10 Chris: procurement note — we'll need standard msla and data processing addendum, i'll send contact info.
06:16 Jordan: thanks everyone. end.

Notes on transcript: some words mis-transcribed (e.g., \"s r e\" for SRE), slight timestamps approximate, speaker labels occasionally first-name-only. Contains natural disfluencies and interruptions.
